lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Costco sells a whole roast chicken for less than it costs to make.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So how does a store that barely profits on groceries get this big?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Start with gross margin: what is left of each dollar after paying for the goods.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Most supermarkets keep around 24 cents. Costco keeps about 13.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The real money is the membership card.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Fee income has climbed every single year, to about 4.8 billion dollars.
lines.spoken: Fee income has climbed every single year, to about four point eight billion dollars.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That is close to all of the profit.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And the card works in every country Costco opens in.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Cheap chicken gets you in the door. The fee keeps the lights on.
